source.title: Empirical Study of Extreme Overfitting Points of Neural Networks

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether networks can reach extreme overfitting using a different data construction: it adds repeatedly duplicated, deliberately corrupted test examples to the training set, then evaluates on the original test set.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for this altered training set, not a training set whose original training labels have all been randomly reassigned. It cites Zhang et al. for fitting random labels; that cited result is not this study's evidence. Weight-distance histograms and the SGD return to good-generalizing points do not measure a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The study uses the random-label memorization finding to construct extreme-overfitting weights. It trains on clean training examples plus duplicated test examples assigned deliberately wrong labels, then evaluates on those same test inputs with their original labels. This does not test fitting completely random training labels, generalization on independent test inputs, a random-corruption sweep, or regularization under the listed random-label conditions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusions: they obtain extreme-overfitting points across the studied datasets, report that these lie farther from initialization than ordinary-training solutions, and state that stochastic gradient descent initialized there usually returns to a good-generalizing point. Their near-zero test accuracy is measured on inputs deliberately included in training with wrong labels.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than randomly relabeling the original training set, the method corrupts test labels, duplicates those examples, appends them to the original training set, and trains on the combined set.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that ResNet overfits faster than the fully connected network. They state that classical stochastic gradient descent did not qualitatively change the experimental results; the plotted experiments use Adam with learning rate 0.001 and batch size 128.

fits_no_version.finding: MLP, LeNet-like CNN and ResNet fit clean training examples combined with duplicated, deliberately mislabeled test examples nearly perfectly, while predicting the original test labels almost entirely incorrectly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks can memorize a mixture of clean examples and deliberately mislabeled examples, including incorrect labels for inputs subsequently evaluated.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors state that L2 regularization does not prevent their constructed extreme-overfitting points, without specifying the experimental settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: L2 regularization can permit extreme overfitting under this duplicated wrong-label construction.

record.problems: The paper describes the accuracy outcomes in text but supplies the per-condition curves as figures without exact reported values. Its corrupted-data construction differs from random relabeling of the original training set, and the text does not specify the L2 experiment's architecture or dataset.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible result rows omitted. Weight-distance histograms and the SGD return from extreme-overfitting weights do not measure a listed version.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling of the training set, near-zero training error under that labeling, chance performance on independent test data, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training-time ratio for random versus true labels and convergence as the corrupted-label fraction increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A sweep of randomly corrupted training labels, perfect training fit throughout, and steadily worsening independent-test performance toward chance.
Whether weight decay, dropout or augmentation prevent fitting random labels, and whether removing explicit regularization harms true-label generalization.
Separate learning trajectories demonstrating that shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: The construction difference and lack of a corruption sweep are untested scope, not evidence warranting limits_scope verdicts. Group-level accuracy statements are supported by the text; exact per-condition endpoints cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not randomly relabel the original training examples: it adds duplicated, deliberately corrupted test examples to the original training set. The test outcome is described as almost zero accuracy, rather than test error at chance, and the experiments use MLP, CNN and ResNet on MNIST, Fashion MNIST and CIFAR 10.

The paper reports an extreme-corruption setup, not a sweep from no corruption to all corruption, so it does not test whether degradation is smooth or whether intermediate noise fractions preserve perfect training fit.

The paper states that adding L2 regularization does not prevent extreme overfitting. It does not report a test of dropout or data augmentation, nor whether removing regularization alone harms generalization on true labels.

rows.operation_detail: Train on original training data combined with duplicated, deliberately corrupted test examples.
rows.measure: Training accuracy on the corrupted training set and accuracy on the original test set
rows.value: Figure only; text describes results across studied models and datasets as close to 100% training accuracy and almost zero test accuracy.
rows.note: The text gives a group-level description, not separate numerical values for this condition.
rows.check: The reported fit concerns clean training data plus duplicated, deliberately mislabeled test inputs. It does not establish V1 or V4; original-test accuracy measures disagreement on inputs included in training.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MLP, CNN and ResNet on MNIST, Fashion MNIST and CIFAR 10 with the paper's corrupted-data construction
reader_labels.reason: The reported extreme fit and poor original-test accuracy support a related memorization result, but the intervention adds corrupted test examples to the original training set rather than randomly relabeling the original training set (R1–R9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Extreme-corruption setup across the reported architectures and datasets
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports the extreme-overfitting endpoint but does not vary corruption fraction to establish smooth degradation or persistent perfect training fit across fractions (R1–R9).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: L2 regularization; architecture and dataset not stated
reader_labels.reason: The authors explicitly state that adding L2 does not prevent finding extreme-overfitting points (R10).
